Q25496853.summary: A crowded frieze of figures in tunics and togas runs along this sarcophagus front. Near the centre Christ stands frontally blessing two baskets of bread held out by disciples, and he appears again in profile touching the eyes of the man born blind, beside Peter (in the guise of Moses) striking water from the rock; at the left an orant, the praying soul of the deceased, is presented to an enthroned teacher. The whole speaks of baptism, Eucharist and the soul's entry into the presence of God.
facts: The panel was found in 1860 in a house on Place Saint-Sernin in Toulouse, where it had been reused as building material.
Its irregular, trapezoidal shape with sloping ends is typical of the early Christian sarcophagi of southwestern Gaul.
The museum notes the sculptor's lively but simplified carving, with drill-work accents and flattened bodies, compared with Roman workshops.
Q25496853.notes: Place of manufacture is inferred from the museum's remark that the shape is typical of southwestern Gaul. The enthroned figure at the left is variously read as Peter teaching or God; scene readings follow the museum's catalogue.
